explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates G-Eval (LLM evaluation) against human annotations on 20 randomly sampled examples, reporting both Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients

prompts.notes: The paper states 'detailed prompts provided in Appendix D' for G-Eval framework evaluation instructions, but exact prompt text is not shown in the provided text

guidelines.notes: Human ratings used 10-point rubrics with specific criteria: Condition Quality (ambiguity capture, distinct interpretations coverage, logical coherence) and Answer Quality (accuracy, completeness, factual soundness)

sample_size.notes: Validation conducted on 20 randomly sampled examples from the full CondAmbigQA benchmark of 2,000 instances

quantitative_scores.notes: Correlation between condition quality and answer performance
Correlation between condition quality and answer performance

validation_results.summary_finding: G-Eval shows strong correlation with human judgments (Pearson: 0.598, Spearman: 0.637, p<0.001), validating its use as an automatic evaluator for ambiguous QA benchmarking.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluation uses automated G-Eval framework with multiple specialized metrics, while human evaluation focuses on the same core quality dimensions but with 10-point rubrics
